payload.reasoning: [1 type; 3 test] Identity, not dependency (Law 8c). T = 1 - S is a definitional identity: the complementary sensitivity function's own accepted definition names the relation 'to sensitivity S(s) = 1 - T(s)' — the two functions are two views of the same closed-loop transfer built from loop gain L, each computed from L, the shared operand. Remove the sensitivity function: nothing stops T being computed and used, because T = L/(1+L) never touches S; the removal merely removes a way of saying it. The note argues exactly this identity — 'T is literally 1 minus S' — which is the constitutive-identity verdict dressed as a removal test; no operational dependency is shown. The correct dependency, if any, is T→loop-gain, the operand both definitions name.

Remove the sensitivity function now and T still computes straight from L — the map's own operation continues, because the map's operand is L, not S. This is the identity-as-definition shape I struck in the transform wave: a derived identity does not show that the map's own operation stops.
